title: 30-second romantic-fantasy drama post-change application
purpose: Same three baseline application scenarios, after the narrowly scoped guidance changes. Verbatim stateless model output; assessment saved separately.

method.engine: eval completion(default), three independent stateless calls

scenario_prompts.romance_approach_stop_eye_contact_reacti: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama: two adult characters approach each other through a moonlit enchanted garden, one stops, they make eye contact, then each reacts. Output a shot-by-shot planning table with seconds, actor blocking, camera movement, action phases, holds/reactions, continuity and AI prompts/handoff. Make it usable for production, but do not assume a reference video.
scenario_prompts.offscreen_entrance_reveal: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama in which one adult character is already in a moonlit hall and a second character enters from offscreen; build a reveal and reaction. Output a shot-by-shot table with seconds, actor blocking, camera movement, action phases, holds/reactions, cut continuity and AI prompt handoff. Be explicit about what is observed versus designed; no reference provided.
scenario_prompts.walk_to_dialogue_interaction: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama: two adult characters walk together through a moonlit garden, transition into a short dialogue interaction, and finish on a reaction. Output shot-by-shot seconds, blocking, camera movement, gait/contact visibility, action phases/cut continuity, holds/reactions and AI prompt handoff. No reference video supplied.

method.scope: No reference video, named generation tool, storyboard images, or rendered clips supplied; outputs are proposals.

**Status:** Design proposal, not based on a reference video. Durations and timing below are proposed shot-local seconds; they are not measured footage or universal motion timings.  
**Assumptions:** Two adult characters, no dialogue specified, one continuous garden location. Character, costume, prop, look IDs and approved reference assets are not supplied. Camera controls and duration limits depend on the selected AI tool and remain unverified.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| **01 · 0–6 s** | Establish the moonlit garden. Both adults are visible at a distance on a clear approach path. They begin walking toward each other. | **Proposal:** Slow, restrained push toward the path; keep both characters readable. | Establish their screen positions and approach directions; carry these into Shot 02. | **Prompt proposal:** “Two adult characters approach along a moonlit enchanted-garden path. Begin with both visible at a distance; one clear, unhurried approach action. End with both still moving toward each other. Preserve garden layout, character appearance, and screen direction.” |
| **02 · 6–12 s** | Continue the approach. One character slows and stops; the other continues only as needed for a readable shared eyeline. | **Proposal:** Gentle tracking with the approaching pair, then settle as the first character stops. | Make the stop legible. | **03 · 12–18 s** | The second character reaches a comfortable stopping distance. Let the shared moment settle into a quiet two-shot and hold the final image. Preserve spacing, gaze, character appearance, and moonlit lighting; add no new action.” |

### Handoff and continuity checks

- Use **shot-local seconds** for this proposal; no FPS or frame counts are specified. Confirm the AI tool’s supported clip lengths, aspect ratio, reference-image inputs, and camera controls before turning the proposal into executable prompts. Do not assume prompt text guarantees a camera move.
- Establish and carry forward character appearance, garden layout, approach direction, stopping distance, eyelines, and lighting. Add approved character/location/look references when available.
- Generate reaction coverage separately if needed to protect eyeline continuity. Review each clip and its cut boundaries for position, gaze, and direction before assembly.
- **Uncertainty:** Exact shot divisions, performance nuance, final framing, camera behavior, and achievable continuity depend on the brief, approved references, and chosen tool. This is a planning proposal, not a generated or verified sequence.
